# RG05 `code-replacement`: The PoC replaces deployed code

<!-- Generated by `realism-gate explain --markdown`. Do not edit by hand. -->

**Severity:** error (error in the exploit; warn in setUp)

`vm.etch` or `deployCodeTo` puts different bytecode at an address the protocol uses.

## Why it matters

Replacing a dependency's code means the PoC no longer runs against the deployed system. Whatever the replacement does, the attacker cannot make the real contract do it. In `setUp()` this is sometimes how a harness installs a test double at a fixed address, which is why it is a warning there; the report then has to show the real dependency behaves the same way.

## How to fix it

Run against the real dependency on a pinned fork. If a double is unavoidable, explain in the report why the real contract can return the same values, and cite where.

## Fires on

```solidity
vm.etch(ORACLE, address(new StaleOracle()).code);
```

## Does not fire on

```solidity
vm.createSelectFork(rpc, BLOCK_WHERE_ORACLE_IS_STALE);
```

## Known false-positive modes

- Etching a precompile or a chain-specific system contract the local EVM lacks. Add an `allow` comment naming it.
- Recreating the attacker's own historical contract at its original address, as post-incident reproductions do. Name the address for what it is (`ATTACKER_CONTRACT`, `exploitHelper`) and the tool treats it as the attacker's.

## Silencing it

Add a comment on the line, or the line above, with a reason:

```solidity
// realism-gate: allow(RG05) <why this is not a defect here>
```

A comment without a reason is ignored, and the output says so.
